rounds.text: Antelopus Selan Energy Ltd trades at an attractive P/E of 19.9x [E1] while delivering explosive fundamentals that vastly outpace the broader sector. Profit growth has compounded at 93% over 5 years [E19, E61] and reached 119% over the trailing twelve months [E21], vastly outstripping the 5-year share price growth of 41% and demonstrating that fundamental performance is severely under-appreciated by the market [E23, E56]. Operating margins have expanded dramatically to 62% in the TTM and hit 70% in June 2026, driven by a consistent 7-year upward trend in profitability [E30, E31, E32]. Furthermore, the company is almost debt free with a negligible debt-to-equity ratio of 0.01x, backed by solid operating cash flows of Rs 121 Cr [E35, E38, E59]. Capital expenditure appears largely complete as evidenced by a 32.7% reduction in capital work-in-progress to Rs 210 Cr, positioning new capacity to come online [E40]. Institutional money flow remains positive alongside a dominant promoter holding of 69.94% [E41, E44], and the stock boasts a perfect relative-strength rating of 100 against the Nifty 500 [E51]. Conceded: free cash flow was negative at Rs -98 Cr in Mar 2026 [E36], debtor days have increased to 88.0 days [E63], and the dividend yield is currently zero [E4, E62].

Conceded: P/E sits at 19.9x [E1]. However, that multiple masks severe cash-generation failure, as free cash flow plunged to a negative Rs -98 Cr in March 2026 despite reported profits [E36]. While the bull points to explosive profit growth of 119% TTM [E21] and expanding margins [E30], operating cash flow was only 78% of operating profit [E37], and debtor days deteriorated from 71.3 to 88.0 days, signaling a dangerous breakdown in working capital collection [E63]. Furthermore, the company offers a 0.00% dividend yield and explicitly faces negative flags from the data provider for withholding payouts despite repeated profits [E4, E62]. The bull highlights massive promoter accumulation [E41], but completely ignores that foreign institutions slashed their holdings down to just 0.41% [E42]. Finally, past price history warns of extreme vulnerability, carrying an annualised volatility of 50.0% and a catastrophic peak-to-trough historical drawdown of -88.9% [E53, E54].
